name: Gertrude Ederle
highlight: First woman across the Channel · Friday 6 August 1926
biography: Gertrude Caroline “Trudy” Ederle was born in New York City on 23 October 1905. A member of the Women’s Swimming Association, she developed into a leading freestyle swimmer before turning to long-distance challenges. At the 1924 Paris Olympics she won gold in the 4 × 100 metres freestyle relay and bronze in both the 100 and 400 metres freestyle.

Ederle turned professional in 1925. On Friday 6 August 1926 she swam from Cap Gris-Nez to Kingsdown, becoming the first woman to cross the English Channel. Her front-crawl crossing was faster than the previous men’s record. The CSA records 14 hours 39 minutes, although some historical accounts give 14 hours 34 minutes.

On 27 August 1926, she returned to New York aboard the Berengaria and was welcomed with a ticker-tape parade. City records preserve the reception committee’s minutes, letters and photographs, including her reception aboard the municipal steamer Macom. The welcome carried her sporting achievement into the city’s civic history.
Later in life, she taught swimming to deaf children, extending her contribution to swimming beyond her competitive achievements.

lines.text: CSA’s 14h39m remains displayed. The museum’s specific entry gives 07:05–21:44 on 6 August 1926; the contemporaneous Capital Journal AP report gives 07:09–21:40 the same day and 14h31m, also reported by TIME. Other historical summaries give 14h34m, and Dover Museum’s general Records and Firsts page prints 14h33m. No signed timing sheet was inspected and no time-standard conversion is inferred.

lines.text: CSA record 2236 and the specific Dover Museum swim entry publish 14:39. The museum supplies 07:05 and 21:44 on 6 August. The original Capital Journal front page of 6 August 1926, in its named Associated Press report, instead gives departure 07:09, landing 21:40 and 14:31. This independently documents a contemporary timing alternative; it does not reconcile the record. The displayed duration and structured clocks retain their CSA/museum attribution, and the result remains disputed.

otherEvents.title: Paris Olympics — women’s 4 × 100 m freestyle relay

lines.text: USA won gold in a team world-record time of 4:58.8; Ederle swam the second leg.

Olympedia’s event table names Ederle in the USA quartet and dates the final to 18 July; its separate world-record chronology instead uses 20 July. The event-table date is shown pending an original-report check. The 4:58.8 is a team time, not her individual split.
